summary: Add a single-repository semcod/regix quality gate command

delivery.outcome: Add `monag quality`: a read-only semcod/regix quality gate (`regix gates`) for exactly one repository. Deliberately refuses workspace mode (--root must be a Git checkout) since regix gates costs roughly a minute per repository (measured ~8-78s depending on cache warmth) -- scanning many repositories the way catalog/audit/export do would take tens of minutes.
nonGoals: monag never invokes a regix write/fix command; only the read-only `gates` subcommand.
No workspace-wide scanning; explicitly refused, not silently slow.
monag does not vendor, install, or require regix; it is an optional external tool.

architecture.decision: New src/monag/quality.py: regix_available()/run_regix()/scan()/markdown(), following the same mockable-subprocess-boundary pattern as export.py's ticket-radar integration. Wire a new `quality` subcommand (not a flag on catalog/export, since its cost/scope model is fundamentally different: single-repository, ~1 minute, not bulk-scannable).
architecture.rollback: Revert the application slice through protected review.

validation.evidence: Quality gate module (workspace-refusal, missing-binary, success, failure, invalid-output) and CLI wiring regression suite passes.
